- **Scope detection** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/scope.go`): `detectScopeBaseRef` returns the first existing ref from the fallback chain `origin/HEAD → origin/main → origin/master → main → master`. Overridable per-invocation via `--base <ref>` (validated through go-git's `ResolveRevision`). `detectScope` (in `cmd.go`) returns the base ref plus a human-facing banner string ("Reviewing feat/X vs main: 3 commits, 7 files changed, 2 uncommitted") for the staging step to fold into the styled prompt.

## Multi-Agent UI

When `RunMulti` is dispatched in a TTY, the sink slice is `[TUISink, DumpSink, SynthesisSink?]`:

- **`TUISink` / `reviewTUIModel`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/tui_sink.go`, `tui_model.go`, `tui_detail.go`): live dashboard with one row per agent (name, status, tokens, last assistant preview, duration). `Ctrl+O` enters drill-in mode on the alt screen showing the full event buffer for the selected agent; `Esc` returns to the dashboard. `Ctrl+C` cancels the run via the shared `CancelFunc`. The model uses `tea.WithoutSignalHandler` so the cobra root retains SIGINT routing. After all agents finish, the user dismisses with any key — `RunFinished` blocks on dismissal so `DumpSink` renders below the TUI rather than overlapping it.
- **`SynthesisSink`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/synthesis_sink.go`): opt-in y/N prompt offered after the dump. On "y", composes a synthesis prompt covering all agent narratives + per-run user prompt, calls the configured summary provider, and prints the unified verdict. Skipped silently when stdin can't prompt, the run was cancelled, or fewer than 2 agents produced usable output. Provider failures degrade gracefully ("synthesis unavailable: <err>") so the user can still commit.
- **Sink composition** (`composeMultiAgentSinks` in `cmd/entire/cli/review/cmd.go`): pure helper taking explicit `isTTY`/`canPrompt` so tests don't depend on real TTY detection. `findTUISink` picks the TUI out of the slice for `Start`/`Wait` lifecycle hooks.
- **Output styling**: `DumpSink` (per-agent findings) and `SynthesisSink` (aggregate verdict) render through `mdrender.RenderMutedForWriter` — a low-chroma palette (`mdrender.mutedStyles`) that keeps coloured+bold headings for structure but neutralises the high-frequency inline noise (inline-code highlight blocks, coloured bullets/links) that makes markdown-dense findings read as a wall of colour. The shared palette (dispatch / explain / status) is untouched. The live TUI dashboard adds no per-cell colour; only its column header is dimmed (`reviewHeaderStyle`, `Faint`).

## Skill Discovery (Claude Code + Codex)

The generic SKILL.md/markdown scanners, version dedupe (`PickLatestVersion`), and frontmatter parsing live in the shared `skilldiscovery` package (`scan.go`), parameterized by an **invocation-form builder** (`SlashForm` for Claude, `DollarForm` for codex) — the only per-agent difference. Each agent's `DiscoverReviewSkills` supplies its roots + form; discovery emits `DiscoveredSkill.Name` already in that agent's invocation form so the shared prompt composer joins it verbatim.

- **Claude Code** (`claudecode/discovery.go`) walks: plugin cache (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/<market>/<plugin>/<version>/{skills,commands,agents}`), user skills (`~/.claude/skills`), user commands/agents (`~/.claude/commands`, `~/.claude/agents`). Emits `/name` / `/plugin:name`.
- **Codex** (`codex/discovery.go`) walks: `~/.codex/skills/<name>`, plugin cache `~/.codex/plugins/cache/<market>/<plugin>/<version>/skills/<name>`, and `~/.codex/superpowers/skills/<name>`. Emits `$name` / `$plugin:name`. Codex has **no curated built-ins** in `skilldiscovery/registry.go` (its review skills are discovered on disk, not bundled in the binary; `/review` is a TUI-only built-in that doesn't fire in `codex exec`).

For the plugin cache, `PickLatestVersion` picks ONE version directory per plugin: highest valid semver wins; if no entries parse as semver, the lexicographic max is picked (handles the `unknown` sentinel some plugins ship, and codex's opaque content-hash version dirs). Without this, multiple installed versions of a plugin produced duplicate skill entries in the picker and prompt.

When an agent has no saved skills and no per-run skill flags, `seedDefaultSkills` (`setup.go`) supplies a default: the agent's curated built-ins, or — for an agent with none (codex) — on-disk discovered skills whose name signals a review skill (contains "review"), so codex still invokes e.g. `$code-reviewer` instead of a generic scope-only prompt. Used by the invoker-only fallback and the `--reviewers` / `--fixer` override.

## Codex specifics (exec fires no hooks)

`codex exec` fires **no lifecycle hooks**, which drives several codex-only behaviors:

- **Skill invocation**: configured skills are passed to codex **verbatim** (no paraphrase) — codex's skill system injects its installed-skill catalog into every exec session and loads the matching `SKILL.md`. Native `codex exec review` is intentionally NOT used (it rejects a prompt under a scope flag and can't carry Entire's scope/per-run/checkpoint context). `codex/reviewer.go` argv: `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --json [-m <model>] [-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>] -`.
- **Live tokens**: `codex exec --json` carries `usage` only on the terminal `turn.completed`, and a review is a single turn — so the TUI would show no tokens until the end. `codex/review_tokens.go` resolves codex's rollout transcript by `thread_id` (from the `thread.started` envelope), **tails it** (via `os.File.Read` — bufio is sticky on EOF), and emits cumulative `Tokens` per `token_count` event. The parser launches the tailer on `thread.started` and uses a `stop` channel + `WaitGroup` so it can't send on a closed channel.
- **Fix manifest sourcing**: because no hook tags a codex review session, `buildLocalReviewManifestFromSummary` includes an agent as a fix source when it has **live output OR a matched session** (not session-match-only) — codex's review narrative is captured in `run.Buffer`. Without this, codex was silently dropped from `entire review fix`. The completion footer prints for a session-less codex-only manifest too; `entire review fix` with no handle resolves to the most-recent run.
- **Skill verification**: `VerifyConfiguredSkillsInstalled` is **advisory for codex** (logs, doesn't block) — codex resolves skills by loose description match, and legacy saved configs may carry pre-`$`form invocations.

## Anti-Features (do NOT recreate)

The redesign eliminated several constructs from the prior implementation. None should be reintroduced without explicit design:

- `PendingReviewMarker` for launchable agents (env-var handshake makes it unnecessary)
- `WorktreePath` field + worktree-scoping logic (env per process eliminates the multi-tenant problem)
- `AgentEntries` map on the marker (each agent has its own env)
- Marker overwrite tripwire / refuse-attach guard (the bug classes they defended against don't exist)
- `--track-only` flag (intentionally removed by #1009)
- `--postreview` / `--finalize` / empty review commits / `/entire-review:finish` skill installer
- `Launcher` + `HeadlessLauncher` as separate interfaces (single `AgentReviewer`)
- Codex chrome-line filtering or any agent-specific stdout post-processing in shared multi-agent code (per-agent parsers own their format; shared code only sees `Event` variants)
- `sync.Once`-guarded onCancel + parallel `signal.Notify` goroutine (single cancel from start)
- Spawn-time multi-select agent picker / `PickAgents` / `PickedAgents` / `multipicker.go` (roles answer "who reviews" up front via `entire review setup`)
- Spawn-time "Choose fix agent" prompt (`FixerOf(s)` is the single source of truth)
- First-run auto-picker on bare `entire review` (replaced by `Run: entire review setup` pointer + invoker-only non-interactive fallback)
- `ConfirmFirstRunSetup` / `RunReviewConfigPicker` (use `RunSetup` instead)
- `MultiPickerFn` on `review.Deps` and the runtime multi-agent picker dispatch fork

NOTE — the unified source⇄findings picker in `entire review fix` (`fix.go`) is **not** a reintroduction of the spawn-time agent picker: it selects which findings to *fix* after a review, not which agents *review*. Reviewer membership is still decided only by roles / `entire review setup`.

## PR #1352 merge — resolved & pushed (`fd871af73..811dc0e09`)

This was the hairy one — `main`'s independent review refactors collided with PR-2's cutover across 8 files. Resolutions (principle: **PR-2's behavior expressed through main's refactored APIs + main's additive features**):

| File | Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `fix.go` / `post_review.go` | PR-2's `launchReviewFixAgent` vs main's extracted `agentlaunch.LaunchFixAgent` | Kept PR-2's `perRunPrompt`; call `agentlaunch.LaunchFixAgent` (the helper main removed) |
| `lifecycle.go` | PR-2's `adoptReviewEnv` vs main's generalized `tryAdoptEnv`+`envAdoptionSpec` (for investigate) | Took main's generalization; behaviorally identical (spawn always sets `=1`) |
| `review_context.go` | PR-2 changed return arity (staging banner) vs main's `gitrepo.OpenPath`/`NewCommittedReadStore` APIs | Kept PR-2's `ContextResult` signature **+** main's git/checkpoint APIs |
| `cmd.go` | PR-2's banner-returning `detectScope` vs main's `out`-printing + `gitrepo.OpenPath` | PR-2's signature + main's `gitrepo.OpenPath` |
| `cmd_test.go` | main adapted dispatch-fork tests PR-2 **deleted** (multipicker) | Took PR-2's tests (theirs referenced 23 deleted symbols) |
| `setup.go` / `picker_test.go` | comment + PR-2's restored-`SaveReviewConfig` tests | Kept PR-2's |
| `CLAUDE.md` | main extracted review docs → `docs/architecture/review-command.md`; PR-2 kept inline | Adopted main's pointer **+** refreshed the extracted doc with PR-2's cutover content |

Plus the import cascade from those API swaps (`os`/`strings` added, unused `agent`/`agenttypes` removed, errors wrapped).

content.text:
This confirms the picture. Here's my honest assessment.

## PR #1352 structure

The 8 commits map to **5 features**, and they fall into two camps by coupling:

**Indivisible core** — all touch `cmd.go` / `setup.go` / `fix.go`:
| Commit | Theme | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `4f79107` | role cutover (flags, delete multipicker, inline prompt, recursion guard, invoker fallback) | +1453/−1104 |
| `0ba1061` | honest live tokens (claude + codex parsers) | +820/−86 |
| `ba16605` | opt-in roles, pre-launch staging, unified fix picker | +682/−157 |

These three can't be split cleanly — they edit the same functions in `cmd.go`/`setup.go`/`fix.go`, and staging/fix-picker *depends on* the cutover. Separating them means conflict-ridden cherry-picks and non-compiling intermediate states.

**Cleanly peelable** — own files, little overlap:
| Commit | Theme | Size | Coupling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `4dab49f` | shared `skilldiscovery` extraction + codex `$name` discovery | +439/−280 | only `scan.go`/`discovery.go` (mechanical refactor) |
| `b3cc058` | muted output (`mdrender`) | +73/−15 | only `mdrender.go` (+ tiny `tui_model` header) |
| `78db6d0` | codex invokes real skill + model/effort | +384/−35 | shares `codex/reviewer.go` with the tokens commit |

## My take

- **Thematically it does make sense as one PR** — it's "make the redesigned `entire review` actually work end-to-end" (the cutover + codex correctness), explicitly framed as PR 2 of 2.
- **But +3905/−1581 across 48 files is a lot to land in one review.** The saving grace is that your 8 commits are already cleanly themed — so the cheapest "split" is to **review it commit-by-commit** (each commit is a coherent unit) rather than re-splitting into separate PRs.
- **Full split is high-cost / low-benefit** because the core trio is genuinely coupled. The only worthwhile peel-offs are `skilldiscovery` (~439 lines, a self-contained refactor reviewers can approve fast) and maybe muted output (~73 lines) — landing those as small standalone PRs *first* would shrink the core by ~500 lines.

So: I'd **not** do a full split, but there's a reasonable middle path. Also — that stray `.antigravitycli/…json` should come out regardless.

message.content: so we use the $ skill discovery for codex specifically instead of slash command is this what you're saying?

content.text:
Yes — exactly. The skill **invocation form is per-agent**, matching the literal token a user would type in each CLI:

- **Claude Code → slash form**: `/review`, `/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr`, `/plugin:name`
- **Codex → dollar form**: `$code-reviewer`, `$plugin:name`

This isn't a different *discovery mechanism* — it's the same shared scanner (`skilldiscovery/scan.go`) walking each agent's on-disk skills, just parameterized by an **invocation-form builder**: `SlashForm` for Claude, `DollarForm` for codex. Each agent's `DiscoverReviewSkills` supplies its roots + form, so discovery emits `DiscoveredSkill.Name` *already in that agent's form*. The shared prompt composer then joins it verbatim.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The reason it's verbatim (no translation): each CLI's skill system parses *its own* token syntax. Codex injects its installed-skill catalog into every `codex exec` session and loads the matching `SKILL.md` when it sees `$name`. Claude does the same with `/name`. So Entire just has to emit the token the target CLI already understands — translating or paraphrasing would *break* the skill match.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Where the legacy concern comes in** (Copilot's #2): a codex config saved *before* this change might still hold a slash-form `/review` (the old codex stub used `/review`). With the new verbatim pass-through, that `/review` goes to codex literally — and since codex expects `$`-form, it won't cleanly match a skill (codex falls back to loose description-matching or a generic scope review). The fix path for a user is to re-run `entire review setup`, which now writes `$`-form for codex.

So the two relevant code surfaces:
- **Discovery + setup** write the correct `$`-form for codex going forward.
- **The reviewer** passes whatever's configured straight through — great for `$`-form, but a stale `/review` is the transitional rough edge.

That's the crux of the open push-back: do we leave stale `/review` to codex's loose-match (my recommendation — it's transitional and the design intends verbatim), or add defensive handling so the codex reviewer skips/normalizes a slash-form token instead of sending it raw? Want me to add that defensive handling?

================= ISSUE entireio/cli#1373 =================
#1373 [OPEN] review: capture model for claude -p reviewer subprocesses (Claude reviewers record empty model)  by peyton-alt
labels: 
--- body ---
## Problem

`entire review` reviewer subprocesses run via `claude -p` do **not** record a model — the per-session checkpoint `metadata.json` lands with `"model": ""`. Codex reviewers (`codex exec`) correctly capture their model (e.g. `gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.5`).

Confirmed on `0.7.4-nightly.202606030753.317a6f99` with a fresh single-agent run (checkpoint `550c766c7ac8`):

```json
{ "agent": "Claude Code", "model": "", "kind": "agent_review",
  "review_skills": ["/review", "/simplify"] }
```

Older runs are inconsistent — some Claude reviewers *did* capture `claude-opus-4-7[1m]` (checkpoint `1047ada4f974`), others empty (`a1589bb9a093`), so it's flaky rather than always-missing.

## Impact

entire.io renders review subagents per-session (PR entirehq/entire.io#2271). Claude reviewer rows show no model badge while Codex rows do — looks inconsistent/broken to users.

## Likely area

Model is set on session state via `StoreModelHint` / `ModelUpdate` (`lifecycle.go`) and read at condense (`manual_commit_condensation.go` `state.ModelName`, with a `sessionStateBackfillModel` fallback). The `claude -p` reviewer path doesn't reliably populate it. Either propagate the model from the reviewer adapter (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/reviewer.go`) or ensure the backfill-from-transcript path runs for review subprocess sessions.

## Acceptance

A fresh mixed `entire review` (Claude + Codex) records a non-empty `model` for **every** reviewer session in the checkpoint metadata.
--- 0 comments ---

content.text:
I've now traced the root cause. Here's the picture.

## How model capture works (and why Claude reviewers are flaky)

A session's `model` reaches checkpoint metadata two ways:
1. **Hooks** — `handleLifecycleModelUpdate` / TurnEnd write `state.ModelName` when the agent's lifecycle events carry a model.
2. **Transcript backfill at condense** — `sessionStateBackfillModel` → `agent.ExtractModel(transcript)`, but only `if state.ModelName == ""`.

- **Codex reviewers work** because they fire *no* hooks, so they always go through path 2, and `ExtractModel` reads the model off the rollout transcript deterministically.
- **Claude `-p` reviewers are flaky** because they're caught between the two: in headless `-p` mode the model-bearing hook events don't fire consistently (path 1 is unreliable), and when path 1 doesn't set it, path 2's backfill isn't reliably landing a model for these subprocess sessions either — hence "sometimes `claude-opus-4-7[1m]`, sometimes empty."

## The clean fix
The Claude reviewer **parser already sees the model** — it decodes `assistant` stream-json envelopes (`{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"…","usage":…}}`) for token counts but currently ignores `message.model`. So the deterministic fix (issue's option a) is to **capture the model in `claudecode/reviewer.go` and propagate it for the review session** — exactly mirroring how codex gets its model from its transcript. That removes the dependency on flaky `-p` hooks. It's agent-layer, so it fits naturally alongside **PR 2 (#1370)**'s "codex/agent review correctness" theme.

## On the FE PR #2271
It looks well-scoped and correct:
- Reads the CLI's existing `kind: "agent_review"` + `review_skills` (no CLI change needed there).
- Author-over-reviewer attribution with a legacy fallback — sensible.
- Correctly defers the Claude model badge to #1373 (and flags the `primary_agent_raw` generated-column follow-up).
- It's in `entirehq/entire.io` (different repo) — I can review the diff/logic but can't build/run it from here.

Checked the code — and the accurate answer is more nuanced (and more important) than what I said:

**It's not review-specific, and it's not "fixers vs reviewers" — it's "did the session change any files."** `lifecycle.go:732`:

```go
if totalChanges == 0 {
    logging.Info(..., "no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint")
    transitionSessionTurnEnd(...); CleanupPrePromptState(...)
    return nil   // ← no SaveStep, no shadow checkpoint
}
```

There is **no `kind`/review exemption** here. So:
- A session that **edits files** → shadow checkpoint → condenses → appears in metadata.
- A session that **edits nothing** → no checkpoint → never condensed → never in metadata.

**Reviewers are read-only by design** (they report findings, don't edit), so a typical reviewer changes no files → it falls into the skip → **it never reaches checkpoint metadata at all.** A *fixer* always edits → always condenses. And a *reviewer* only shows up if its skills happened to edit (the issue's example had `/simplify`, which edits code — that's why *that* reviewer condensed, with `model=""`).

So, directly answering you: I shouldn't say "all reviewers never condense" — I should say **"any session that changes no files doesn't condense, and reviewers are normally read-only, so most reviewer sessions won't appear in checkpoint metadata."**

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is bigger than #1373. The model bug only matters for reviewers that *also edited*. But the FE PR (#2271) wants to surface review subagents generally — and a pure analysis-only reviewer is invisible to it, because it's never recorded. If the intent is "every reviewer is attributed," the real fix is to **record review sessions even when they touch no files** (exempt `kind=agent_review` from the no-files skip, or capture them another way) — and #1373's model fix only becomes fully meaningful once read-only reviewers are recorded.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

content.text:
I've found the root of it — and it's a real regression, not intended behavior. Here's the full chain:

## The actual gap

**Read-only review sessions are never recorded in checkpoint metadata at all.** The mechanism:

1. A review session is tagged `Kind=agent_review` in *session state* (via `adoptReviewEnv`).
2. That tag only reaches *checkpoint metadata* at **condense** (`condensation.go:245-249` writes `Kind`/`ReviewSkills`/`HasReview`).
3. Condense only processes a session that created a **shadow checkpoint**.
4. A session that changed no files is skipped at `TurnEnd` (`lifecycle.go:732`) with **no review exemption** → no shadow checkpoint → never condensed → the `agent_review` tag (and model) are never persisted.

I confirmed there's **no review-specific checkpoint creation** anywhere (`review/*.go` has no `SaveStep`; the lifecycle has no `Kind==review` bypass).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is a **regression from the redesign**. CLAUDE.md's anti-features list shows the old design recorded reviews via **empty review commits** (`--postreview`/`--finalize`/empty commits — deliberately removed). The new design replaced that with "condense the review session into the next checkpoint" — but a read-only review has *nothing to condense*, so the recording silently dropped. Reviewers only survive into metadata if their skills happened to **edit files** (the issue's example had `/simplify`, which edits — that's why it appeared, with `model=""`). Pure analysis-only reviews vanish entirely.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## What this means
- **#1373's model fix is correct but secondary.** It only manifests for reviews that *do* condense (i.e., touched files). For read-only reviews, there's no metadata row to put a model on.
- **The FE PR (#2271) can't surface read-only reviewers** — they're not in the data. It'll only show reviewers that edited.
- **The prerequisite fix** is to record review sessions even when they change no files — e.g., exempt `kind=agent_review` (and `investigate`) from the no-files skip so they produce a minimal checkpoint capturing the review fact + transcript (+ model). That makes #1373 meaningful *and* makes the FE feature work for all reviews.

So the real work is bigger than the model field. How do you want to proceed?

content.text:
You're right, and I walked too far with the "reviews are never recorded" claim — let me correct it. I read the data model:

**All the per-subagent review data lives in one place — `CommittedMetadata`, written at condense** (`checkpoint.go`): `Agent`, `Prompts`, `Kind`, `ReviewSkills`, `ReviewPrompt`, **and `Model`**. So a review session that's recorded has *all* of these; `model` isn't returned through a different path than agent/prompt — it's the same `metadata.json`. The difference is just whether `state.ModelName` was populated before condense:

- **Codex** sets it: codex's lifecycle events carry the model (`codex/lifecycle.go` → `Model: raw.Model`), so `state.ModelName` is populated → it lands in metadata.
- **Claude `-p`** doesn't reliably: its headless hooks flakily carry the model (hence the issue's "sometimes opus-4-7, sometimes empty"), and Claude had **no transcript fallback** — so when the hook misses, `model=""`.

So my `ExtractModel` fix is actually the *right* shape for what you described: it makes Claude's model get captured **at the same point and into the same metadata as agent/prompt** — by reading it off the transcript at condense when the hook missed it (exactly how `pi` works). And I did prove that part end-to-end: a real Claude session that landed with `model=None` was backfilled to `claude-opus-4-8` in the actual condensed `metadata.json`.

Where I overreached: claiming read-only reviews "never condense / aren't recorded." You've seen them in the UI, so they do condense in normal use — my isolated smoke's review session happened not to (it had no shadow checkpoint), but that's not the universal rule I made it out to be, and it's a separate matter from the model field.

So the model fix stands and matches your framing. Two things I want your read on before I commit:

1. The fix captures the **actual** model the agent used (from the transcript). The alternative — threading model through the `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*` env like skills/prompt — doesn't work cleanly because the parent doesn't know what model `claude -p` will pick. Agree the transcript-backfill is the right source?
2. Want me to drop the integration test (per your earlier preference) and just commit the fix, given the real-run proof already showed `None → claude-opus-4-8` in actual checkpoint metadata?

entire.io's per-reviewer attribution (entirehq/entire.io#2271).

hook's context-window variant ("claude-opus-4-7[1m]"), so backfilled models
